16"""Triton ``multilabel_margin_loss`` for the H20-3e / CUDA target. 

17 

18Contract, established by target-side probes of ``aten::multilabel_margin_loss`` 

19(geometry, out-overload resize/alias, reduction fallback, dtype acceptance, 

20non-contiguous strides, gradient formula) and by the frozen FlagGems pytest: 

21 

22* ``self`` is an (N, C) float matrix, or a rank<=1 single C-class row; ``target`` 

23 is int64 of exactly the same shape, listing active class ids terminated by the 

24 first ``-1``. 

25* Per row: ``A`` = active entries (duplicates kept, entries after the first -1 

26 ignored); ``S`` = set of class ids in ``A``; ``NT`` = classes not in ``S``. 

27 ``row_loss = (1/C) * sum_{j in A} sum_{d in NT} relu(1 - x[target[j]] + x[d])``. 

28 Evaluating the pair set instead of the reference's per-j masked sum is an 

29 exact re-association of the same finite sum. 

30* The native CUDA kernel evaluates the hinge expression in the *input* dtype 

31 (probed: only that form reproduces its saturating half-precision rows on the 

32 extreme-magnitude pytest ranges), sums the resulting terms in at::acc_type 

33 (fp32 for fp16/bf16/fp32, fp64 for fp64), and scales by 1/C in that 

34 accumulator. This module does the same; the single rounding to the output 

35 dtype happens at the final store. Reductions 1 and 2 likewise accumulate the 

36 per-row losses in at::acc_type without an intermediate per-row rounding 

37 (probed on a 300-case fp16 sweep: the native scalar matches an acc_type 

38 accumulation of the unrounded rows, not a sum of fp16-rounded rows). 

39* An id outside ``[0, C)`` is garbage input that the native kernel indexes with 

40 unchecked -- probed on CUDA, an id of 5 against C=3 returns a value built from 

41 memory past the row instead of raising -- so it is not validated here either. 

42 What this module guarantees is memory safety: every indirect address is 

43 clamped into the row while the target/non-target masks keep using the raw id, 

44 so an out-of-range id contributes no hinge pair on any path. A validating 

45 kernel was considered and rejected: raising requires a device-to-host sync of 

46 the flag, and that sync cannot be captured in a CUDA graph (probed: the 

47 existing ``multilabel_margin_loss_forward``, which does validate this way, 

48 fails ``torch.cuda.graph`` capture with ``cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated``). 

49* reduction 0 -> per-row losses; 1 -> mean over rows; anything else (2, and also 

50 -1/3, which the native kernel treats as sum) -> sum over rows. 

51* rank<=1 inputs produce a 0-dim result for every reduction; output dtype is the 

52 input dtype; N == 0 produces an empty (0,) result for *every* reduction, not 

53 only for 0 (probed on CUDA: reductions 1 and 2 also return shape (0,) on a 

54 (0, 11) input, so neither the 0-dim nan of a mean nor the 0-dim zero of a sum 

55 appears here). 

56* ``.out`` overload: positional ``reduction``, keyword-only ``out``; the buffer is 

57 resized to the result shape, written in place and returned. Any floating 

58 ``out`` dtype is accepted, matching the native overload, which casts into the 

59 buffer rather than requiring the input dtype (probed: an fp16 and an fp64 

60 buffer both accept an fp32 input). 

61* Non-contiguous strided inputs are handled through explicit strides. 

62* The allocating overload is differentiable; the gradient is produced by the 

63 Triton kernels below. Writing ``m[d]`` for the number of times class ``d`` 

64 occurs in ``A``, the native gradient for ``d`` in ``S`` is 

65 ``-m[d] * #{k in NT : 1 - x[d] + x[k] > 0}`` and for ``d`` in ``NT`` it is 

66 ``+sum_{k in S} m[k] * [1 - x[k] + x[d] > 0]``, scaled by ``1/(C*N)`` for the 

67 mean. The ``m`` factors are what make a duplicated target id count once per 

68 entry: probed on CUDA, ``C=3``, ``target=[0, 0, -1]`` has native gradient 

69 ``[-4/3, 2/3, 2/3]``, twice the single-entry value. 

70 

71The class axis of a row is split across a 2D ``(rows, n_class_tiles)`` grid so the 

72benchmark's few-row / large-C shapes still cover the whole device; when a row has 

73exactly one class tile the finish step is folded into the row-loss kernel. 

74 

75All numerical work happens in the Triton kernels; the host wrapper only does 

76metadata math, allocation, launches and the autograd plumbing that selects them. 

77"""

84

88logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

90_FLOAT_DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64) 

91 

92_REDUCE_BLOCK = 2048 

93_FINISH_BLOCK = 256 

94_BLOCK_T = 256 

95_BLOCK_C = 64 

96_BLOCK_J = 16 

97# Class counts up to this size are handled by one program per row (a single 

98# launch, no partial buffer) for reduction 0, which saves the partial buffer and 

99# the second launch whenever the row still fits a single tile. 

100_R0_SINGLE_TILE_MAX = 4096 

101# The outer-product path materialises a BLOCK_J x BLOCK_C tile, so the 

102# single-tile BLOCK_C is capped to keep that tile inside the register budget: 

103# 16 x 4096 fp64 would be 512KB per program and spills. Rows wider than the cap 

104# fall back to the split grid, which tiles the class axis at _BLOCK_C instead. 

105_R0_SINGLE_TILE_BLOCK_CAP = 2048 

106_R0_SINGLE_TILE_BLOCK_CAP_FP64 = 1024 

107_GRAD_BLOCK_D = 32 

108_GRAD_BLOCK_K = 64

114@triton.jit 

115def _safe_class_index(ids, C): 

116 """Clamp a loaded class id into [0, C) for address arithmetic only. 

117 

118 A target id outside ``[0, C)`` is garbage input: the native kernel indexes 

119 with it unchecked and reads whatever lies past the row (probed on CUDA: an 

120 id of 5 against C=3 returns a value built from out-of-row memory rather than 

121 raising). Reproducing an out-of-range read is not an option here, so every 

122 indirect load is clamped instead. The clamp feeds the *address* only; the 

123 target/non-target masks are still derived from the raw id, so an 

124 out-of-range id contributes no hinge pair on either path. 

125 """ 

126 return tl.minimum(tl.maximum(ids.to(tl.int32), 0), C - 1)

129@libentry() 

130@triton.jit 

131def _row_loss_kernel( 

132 x_ptr, 

133 t_ptr, 

134 o_ptr, 

135 N, 

136 C, 

137 cstride, 

138 n_ct, 

139 srs, 

140 scs, 

141 trs, 

142 tcs, 

143 ACC64: tl.constexpr, 

144 FINAL: tl.constexpr, 

145 BLOCK_T: tl.constexpr, 

146 BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr, 

147 BLOCK_J: tl.constexpr, 

148): 

149 """Partial (or final) ``sum_{j in A} sum_{d in NT} relu(1 - x[t[j]] + x[d])``. 

150 

151 One program per (row, class tile) pair, so a few-row / large-C shape still 

152 fills the device. ``FINAL`` (single class tile) writes ``total / C`` to 

153 ``o_ptr[row]``; otherwise the raw partial goes to ``o_ptr[row * cstride + 

154 pid_c]`` and ``_finish_kernel`` folds the per-row tiles. A row whose active 

155 target prefix has exactly one entry takes a vector-width path that evaluates 

156 only the real pairs, and class tiles holding no non-target class are skipped 

157 entirely (which collapses the all-targets case). 

158 """ 

159 row = tl.program_id(0) 

160 pid_c = tl.program_id(1) 

161 bx = row * srs 

162 bt = row * trs 

163 stop = C 

164 for t0 in range(0, C, BLOCK_T): 

165 offs = t0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_T) 

166 m = offs < C 

167 tb = tl.load(t_ptr + bt + offs * tcs, mask=m, other=-1) 

168 stop = tl.minimum(stop, tl.min(tl.where(m & (tb < 0), offs, C), axis=0)) 

169 if ACC64: 

170 tot = tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.float64) 

171 else: 

172 tot = tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.float32) 

173 for c0 in range(pid_c * BLOCK_C, C, n_ct * BLOCK_C): 

174 offs = c0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_C) 

175 cm = offs < C 

176 xd = tl.load(x_ptr + bx + offs * scs, mask=cm, other=0.0) 

177 if stop == 1: 

178 # Exactly one active target: the target set is that single id, so the 

179 # whole pair tile collapses to one BLOCK_C-wide vector instead of a 

180 # BLOCK_J x BLOCK_C outer product that would spend 15/16 of its lanes 

181 # on padding. 

182 raw0 = tl.load(t_ptr + bt) 

183 id0 = _safe_class_index(raw0, C) 

184 in_range0 = (raw0 >= 0) & (raw0 < C) 

185 xj = tl.load(x_ptr + bx + id0 * scs) 

186 # Hinge in the input element type, exactly as the native CUDA kernel. 

187 marg = (1.0 - xj) + xd 

188 # The non-target set excludes the raw id, so an out-of-range id 

189 # leaves the whole tile inactive exactly as it does below. 

190 keep = cm & in_range0 & (offs != raw0) & (marg > 0.0) 

191 if ACC64: 

192 tot += tl.sum(tl.where(keep, marg, 0.0), axis=0) 

193 else: 

194 tot += tl.sum(tl.where(keep, marg.to(tl.float32), 0.0), axis=0) 

195 else: 

196 mem = tl.zeros((BLOCK_C,), dtype=tl.int32) 

197 for j0 in range(0, stop, BLOCK_J): 

198 jj = j0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_J) 

199 jm = jj < stop 

200 ids = tl.load(t_ptr + bt + jj * tcs, mask=jm, other=-2) 

201 mem += tl.sum( 

202 ((ids[:, None] == offs[None, :]) & jm[:, None]).to(tl.int32), 

203 axis=0, 

204 ) 

205 nt = cm & (mem == 0) 

206 if tl.sum(nt.to(tl.int32), axis=0) != 0: 

207 for j0 in range(0, stop, BLOCK_J): 

208 jj = j0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_J) 

209 jm = jj < stop 

210 raw = tl.load(t_ptr + bt + jj * tcs, mask=jm, other=-2) 

211 # Masks come from the raw id, addresses from the clamp. 

212 jm = jm & (raw >= 0) & (raw < C) 

213 xj = tl.load( 

214 x_ptr + bx + _safe_class_index(raw, C) * scs, 

215 mask=jm, 

216 other=0.0, 

217 ) 

218 # Hinge in the input element type, exactly as the native CUDA 

219 # kernel: rounding the margin back to the element type before 

220 # the accumulation reproduces its saturating fp16 rows. 

221 marg = (1.0 - xj)[:, None] + xd[None, :] 

222 keep = jm[:, None] & nt[None, :] 

223 if ACC64: 

224 tot += tl.sum( 

225 tl.sum(tl.where(keep & (marg > 0.0), marg, 0.0), axis=1), 

226 axis=0, 

227 ) 

228 else: 

229 tot += tl.sum( 

230 tl.sum( 

231 tl.where(keep & (marg > 0.0), marg.to(tl.float32), 0.0), 

232 axis=1, 

233 ), 

234 axis=0, 

235 ) 

236 if FINAL: 

237 tl.store(o_ptr + row, (tot / C).to(o_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

238 else: 

239 tl.store(o_ptr + row * cstride + pid_c, tot)

242@libentry() 

243@triton.jit 

244def _finish_kernel( 

245 part_ptr, 

246 out_ptr, 

247 C, 

248 n_ct, 

249 ACC64: tl.constexpr, 

250 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

251): 

252 """Fold the per-class-tile partials of one row and apply the 1/C scale.""" 

253 row = tl.program_id(0) 

254 if ACC64: 

255 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float64) 

256 else: 

257 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32) 

258 for c0 in range(0, n_ct, BLOCK): 

259 offs = c0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

260 v = tl.load(part_ptr + row * n_ct + offs, mask=offs < n_ct, other=0.0) 

261 acc += v 

262 tl.store(out_ptr + row, (tl.sum(acc, axis=0) / C).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))

265@libentry() 

266@triton.jit 

267def _reduce_rows_kernel( 

268 rows_ptr, 

269 out_ptr, 

270 N, 

271 MEAN: tl.constexpr, 

272 ACC64: tl.constexpr, 

273 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

274): 

275 """Vectorised tree reduction of the per-row losses into one scalar.""" 

276 if ACC64: 

277 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float64) 

278 else: 

279 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32) 

280 for r0 in range(0, N, BLOCK): 

281 offs = r0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

282 v = tl.load(rows_ptr + offs, mask=offs < N, other=0.0) 

283 acc += v 

284 total = tl.sum(acc, axis=0) 

285 if MEAN: 

286 total = total / N 

287 tl.store(out_ptr, total.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))

293@libentry() 

294@triton.jit 

295def _membership_kernel( 

296 t_ptr, 

297 m_ptr, 

298 C, 

299 trs, 

300 tcs, 

301 BLOCK_T: tl.constexpr, 

302 BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr, 

303): 

304 """Multiplicity of every class id inside the active target prefix of a row.""" 

305 row = tl.program_id(0) 

306 bt = row * trs 

307 stop = C 

308 for t0 in range(0, C, BLOCK_T): 

309 offs = t0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_T) 

310 m = offs < C 

311 tb = tl.load(t_ptr + bt + offs * tcs, mask=m, other=-1) 

312 stop = tl.minimum(stop, tl.min(tl.where(m & (tb < 0), offs, C), axis=0)) 

313 for c0 in range(0, C, BLOCK_C): 

314 offs = c0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_C) 

315 cm = offs < C 

316 cnt = tl.zeros((BLOCK_C,), dtype=tl.int32) 

317 for t0 in range(0, stop, BLOCK_T): 

318 jj = t0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_T) 

319 jm = jj < stop 

320 ids = tl.load(t_ptr + bt + jj * tcs, mask=jm, other=-2) 

321 cnt += tl.sum( 

322 ((ids[:, None] == offs[None, :]) & jm[:, None]).to(tl.int32), axis=0 

323 ) 

324 tl.store(m_ptr + row * C + offs, cnt, mask=cm)

327@libentry() 

328@triton.jit 

329def _grad_kernel( 

330 x_ptr, 

331 m_ptr, 

332 g_ptr, 

333 go_ptr, 

334 C, 

335 srs, 

336 scs, 

337 gos, 

338 n_mean, 

339 ACC64: tl.constexpr, 

340 BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr, 

341 BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr, 

342): 

343 """d(loss)/dx for one (row, class tile), written once in the output dtype. 

344 

345 Each class ``d`` of the tile gets its own complete reduction over the whole 

346 class axis, so the tile is the only writer of its slice and no atomics or 

347 zero-initialised buffer are needed: 

348 

349 * ``d`` in ``S``: ``-m[d] * #{k in NT : 1 - x[d] + x[k] > 0}``. The ``m[d]`` 

350 factor is what makes a duplicated target id contribute once per *entry*, 

351 matching the native kernel, which walks the target prefix and subtracts 

352 the hinge count again for every repeat of the id. 

353 * ``d`` in ``NT``: ``sum_{k in S} m[k] * [1 - x[k] + x[d] > 0]``, i.e. one 

354 count per active target entry, duplicates included. 

355 

356 Both reductions are evaluated for every ``d`` and selected at the end, which 

357 keeps the tile branch-free. The hinge is compared in the input element type, 

358 as in the forward kernel, and the accumulator is ``at::acc_type``. 

359 

360 ``n_mean`` is the row count for reduction 1 and 1 otherwise; the ``1/(C * 

361 n_mean)`` scale is formed here rather than passed in, because a host-side 

362 Python float binds to an fp32 kernel slot and would cap the fp64 gradient at 

363 fp32 precision. 

364 """ 

365 row = tl.program_id(0) 

366 pid_d = tl.program_id(1) 

367 bx = row * srs 

368 rb = row * C 

369 if ACC64: 

370 acc_ty: tl.constexpr = tl.float64 

371 else: 

372 acc_ty: tl.constexpr = tl.float32 

373 # tl.full rather than ``.to``: a value Triton specialises to a literal 1 

374 # arrives as a Python int, which has no ``.to``. Forming the scale here 

375 # rather than taking it as a host float matters for fp64, whose gradient 

376 # would otherwise be capped at the fp32 precision of the argument slot. 

377 scale = 1.0 / (tl.full((), 1.0, dtype=acc_ty) * C * n_mean) 

378 # ``gos`` is 0 for a scalar upstream gradient, so the same expression reads 

379 # the single element for reductions 1 and 2 and the per-row element for 

380 # reduction 0, at whatever stride the caller's view has. 

381 factor = tl.load(go_ptr + row * gos).to(acc_ty) 

382 offs_d = pid_d * BLOCK_D + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D) 

383 cm_d = offs_d < C 

384 md = tl.load(m_ptr + rb + offs_d, mask=cm_d, other=0) 

385 xd = tl.load(x_ptr + bx + offs_d * scs, mask=cm_d, other=0.0) 

386 cnt_t = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=acc_ty) 

387 cnt_n = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=acc_ty) 

388 for k0 in range(0, C, BLOCK_K): 

389 offs_k = k0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K) 

390 cm_k = offs_k < C 

391 mk = tl.load(m_ptr + rb + offs_k, mask=cm_k, other=0) 

392 xk = tl.load(x_ptr + bx + offs_k * scs, mask=cm_k, other=0.0) 

393 nt_k = cm_k & (mk == 0) 

394 is_t_k = cm_k & (mk > 0) 

395 # d plays the target, k the non-target class. 

396 hit_t = (((1.0 - xd)[:, None] + xk[None, :]) > 0.0) & nt_k[None, :] 

397 # k plays the target, d the non-target class. 

398 hit_n = (((1.0 - xk)[None, :] + xd[:, None]) > 0.0) & is_t_k[None, :] 

399 cnt_t += tl.sum(tl.where(hit_t, 1.0, 0.0), axis=1) 

400 cnt_n += tl.sum(tl.where(hit_n, mk.to(acc_ty)[None, :], 0.0), axis=1) 

401 g = tl.where(md > 0, -md.to(acc_ty) * cnt_t, cnt_n) * (scale * factor) 

402 tl.store(g_ptr + rb + offs_d, g.to(g_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=cm_d)

408def _strides2d(t): 

409 """(row_stride, class_stride) for a rank<=2 tensor viewed as (rows, classes).""" 

410 if t.dim() == 0: 

411 return 1, 1 

412 if t.dim() == 1: 

413 return 0, t.stride(0) 

414 return t.stride(0), t.stride(1) 

415 

416 

417def _row_col(t): 

418 if t.dim() == 0: 

419 return 1, 1 

420 if t.dim() == 1: 

421 return 1, int(t.shape[0]) 

422 return int(t.shape[0]), int(t.shape[1]) 

423 

424 

425def _result_shape(rows, reduction, rank_leq_1): 

426 if rows == 0: 

427 return (0,) 

428 if reduction == 0 and not rank_leq_1: 

429 return (rows,) 

430 return ()

433def _row_losses(self, target, dest): 

434 """Write the per-row losses (already divided by C) into ``dest``. 

435 

436 The class axis is split across ``n_ct`` programs per row, so the benchmark's 

437 few-row shapes still cover the whole device; when a row spans a single class 

438 tile the 1/C fold is done inside the row kernel and no partial buffer or 

439 second launch is needed. 

440 """ 

441 rows, n_classes = _row_col(self) 

442 acc64 = self.dtype == torch.float64 

443 acc_dtype = torch.float64 if acc64 else torch.float32 

444 srs, scs = _strides2d(self) 

445 trs, tcs = _strides2d(target) 

446 n_ct = -(-n_classes // _BLOCK_C) 

447 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

448 if n_ct == 1: 

449 _row_loss_kernel[(rows, 1)]( 

450 self, 

451 target, 

452 dest, 

453 rows, 

454 n_classes, 

455 1, 

456 1, 

457 srs, 

458 scs, 

459 trs, 

460 tcs, 

461 ACC64=acc64, 

462 FINAL=True, 

463 BLOCK_T=_BLOCK_T, 

464 BLOCK_C=_BLOCK_C, 

465 BLOCK_J=_BLOCK_J, 

466 ) 

467 return 

468 part = torch.empty((rows, n_ct), dtype=acc_dtype, device=self.device) 

469 _row_loss_kernel[(rows, n_ct)]( 

470 self, 

471 target, 

472 part, 

473 rows, 

474 n_classes, 

475 n_ct, 

476 n_ct, 

477 srs, 

478 scs, 

479 trs, 

480 tcs, 

481 ACC64=acc64, 

482 FINAL=False, 

483 BLOCK_T=_BLOCK_T, 

484 BLOCK_C=_BLOCK_C, 

485 BLOCK_J=_BLOCK_J, 

486 ) 

487 _finish_kernel[(rows,)]( 

488 part, 

489 dest, 

490 n_classes, 

491 n_ct, 

492 ACC64=acc64, 

493 BLOCK=_FINISH_BLOCK, 

494 )

497def _launch_forward(self, target, reduction, dest): 

498 """Run the forward kernels and write the requested reduction into ``dest``. 

499 

500 Reduction 0 (a (rows,) result) whose class axis fits one capped tile is 

501 computed by a single launch covering the whole axis, which saves the partial 

502 buffer and the second launch. The cap keeps the BLOCK_J x BLOCK_C pair tile 

503 inside the register budget (it is tighter for fp64, whose elements are twice 

504 as wide); wider rows -- and every scalar reduction -- take the split grid. 

505 """ 

506 rows, n_classes = _row_col(self) 

507 acc64 = self.dtype == torch.float64 

508 acc_dtype = torch.float64 if acc64 else torch.float32 

509 srs, scs = _strides2d(self) 

510 trs, tcs = _strides2d(target) 

511 block_cap = _R0_SINGLE_TILE_BLOCK_CAP_FP64 if acc64 else _R0_SINGLE_TILE_BLOCK_CAP 

512 single_tile_max = min(_R0_SINGLE_TILE_MAX, block_cap) 

513 if reduction == 0 and not (self.dim() <= 1) and n_classes <= single_tile_max: 

514 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

515 _row_loss_kernel[(rows, 1)]( 

516 self, 

517 target, 

518 dest, 

519 rows, 

520 n_classes, 

521 1, 

522 1, 

523 srs, 

524 scs, 

525 trs, 

526 tcs, 

527 ACC64=acc64, 

528 FINAL=True, 

529 BLOCK_T=_BLOCK_T, 

530 BLOCK_C=triton.next_power_of_2(n_classes), 

531 BLOCK_J=_BLOCK_J, 

532 ) 

533 return 

534 if reduction == 0 and not (self.dim() <= 1): 

535 _row_losses(self, target, dest) 

536 return 

537 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

538 row_buf = torch.empty(rows, dtype=acc_dtype, device=self.device) 

539 _row_losses(self, target, row_buf) 

540 _reduce_rows_kernel[(1,)]( 

541 row_buf, 

542 dest, 

543 rows, 

544 MEAN=(reduction == 1), 

545 ACC64=acc64, 

546 BLOCK=_REDUCE_BLOCK, 

547 ) 

548 

549 

550def _launch_backward(self, target, reduction, grad_out): 

551 """Gradient of the loss w.r.t. ``self``, produced by the kernels above. 

552 

553 ``g`` is allocated in the input dtype and each class tile stores its slice 

554 exactly once, so the gradient needs no accumulator buffer, no atomics and no 

555 host-side cast. ``grad_out`` is read through its own stride rather than 

556 being made contiguous first, so a strided upstream gradient costs no copy. 

557 """ 

558 rows, n_classes = _row_col(self) 

559 acc64 = self.dtype == torch.float64 

560 device = self.device 

561 srs, scs = _strides2d(self) 

562 trs, tcs = _strides2d(target) 

563 # Passed as an integer so the kernel can build the scale in its own 

564 # accumulator precision; a host float would arrive as fp32. 

565 n_mean = rows if reduction == 1 else 1 

566 # A 0-dim upstream gradient (reductions 1 and 2, and rank<=1 at reduction 0) 

567 # is read by every row, which stride 0 expresses directly; a per-row one is 

568 # read at its own stride, so a strided view costs no copy. 

569 gos = grad_out.stride(0) if grad_out.dim() == 1 else 0 

570 with torch_device_fn.device(device): 

571 mult = torch.empty((rows, n_classes), dtype=torch.int32, device=device) 

572 _membership_kernel[(rows,)]( 

573 target, 

574 mult, 

575 n_classes, 

576 trs, 

577 tcs, 

578 BLOCK_T=_BLOCK_T, 

579 BLOCK_C=_BLOCK_C, 

580 ) 

581 g = torch.empty((rows, n_classes), dtype=self.dtype, device=device) 

582 _grad_kernel[(rows, triton.cdiv(n_classes, _GRAD_BLOCK_D))]( 

583 self, 

584 mult, 

585 g, 

586 grad_out, 

587 n_classes, 

588 srs, 

589 scs, 

590 gos, 

591 n_mean, 

592 ACC64=acc64, 

593 BLOCK_D=_GRAD_BLOCK_D, 

594 BLOCK_K=_GRAD_BLOCK_K, 

595 ) 

596 return g.reshape(self.shape) 

597 

598 

599class _MMLFunction(torch.autograd.Function): 

600 """Autograd wrapper so the allocating overload stays differentiable.""" 

601 

602 @staticmethod 

603 def forward(ctx, x, target, reduction): 

604 rows, _ = _row_col(x) 

605 result = torch.empty( 

606 _result_shape(rows, reduction, x.dim() <= 1), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device 

607 ) 

608 _launch_forward(x, target, reduction, result) 

609 ctx.reduction = reduction 

610 ctx.save_for_backward(x, target) 

611 return result 

612 

613 @staticmethod 

614 def backward(ctx, grad_out): 

615 x, target = ctx.saved_tensors 

616 return _launch_backward(x, target, ctx.reduction, grad_out), None, None 

617 

618 

619def multilabel_margin_loss(self, target, reduction=1, out=None): 

620 logger.debug("GEMS MULTILABEL_MARGIN_LOSS") 

621 if isinstance(reduction, bool) or not isinstance(reduction, int): 

622 raise RuntimeError( 

623 "multilabel_margin_loss: reduction must be an integer (0, 1 or 2)" 

624 ) 

625 if reduction not in (0, 1, 2): 

626 # The native kernel maps every other integer to "sum". 

627 reduction = 2 

628 

629 ndim = self.dim() 

630 if ndim > 2: 

631 raise RuntimeError("multilabel_margin_loss: input must be scalar, 1D or 2D") 

632 if tuple(self.shape) != tuple(target.shape): 

633 raise RuntimeError( 

634 "multilabel_margin_loss: target shape must exactly match input shape" 

635 ) 

636 if self.device != target.device: 

637 raise RuntimeError( 

638 "multilabel_margin_loss: input and target must be on the same device" 

639 ) 

640 if target.dtype != torch.int64: 

641 raise RuntimeError("multilabel_margin_loss: target must have dtype int64") 

642 if self.dtype not in _FLOAT_DTYPES: 

643 raise RuntimeError( 

644 "multilabel_margin_loss: input must have a floating point dtype" 

645 ) 

646 

647 rows, n_classes = _row_col(self) 

648 if n_classes == 0: 

649 raise RuntimeError("multilabel_margin_loss: class dimension must be non-empty") 

650 

651 rank_leq_1 = ndim <= 1 

652 shape = _result_shape(rows, reduction, rank_leq_1) 

653 

654 if out is not None: 

655 if out.device != self.device: 

656 raise RuntimeError( 

657 "multilabel_margin_loss: out must be on the same device as input" 

658 ) 

659 if out.dtype not in _FLOAT_DTYPES: 

660 raise RuntimeError( 

661 "multilabel_margin_loss: out must have a floating point dtype" 

662 ) 

663 if tuple(out.shape) != tuple(shape): 

664 out.resize_(shape) 

665 if rows != 0: 

666 # The native overload writes the result contiguously from the 

667 # buffer's base regardless of the buffer's strides (probed on CUDA: 

668 # a (8,) stride-2 out at reduction 0 received all eight per-row 

669 # values in consecutive storage slots, so its logical view read back 

670 # [r0, r2, r4, r6, fill, fill, fill, fill]). Writing through the 

671 # kernel's flat indexing reproduces that, so no stride handling is 

672 # added here; see the note in the test module. 

673 _launch_forward(self, target, reduction, out) 

674 return out 

675 

676 if rows == 0: 

677 return torch.empty((0,), dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device) 

678 

679 if self.requires_grad and torch.is_grad_enabled(): 

680 return _MMLFunction.apply(self, target, reduction) 

681 

682 result = torch.empty(shape, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device) 

683 _launch_forward(self, target, reduction, result) 

684 return result
